page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. A running head and page number at the top. A decorative woodcut initial N at the left beside the first lines. A centred heading above the text, a centred italic subheading in the middle, and a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.l: NONVM PRÆCEPTVM.

l.i: Scopus aut finis huius præcepti est sanctio

main_text.l: nes. Neque tantum prohibetur in
hoc præcepto falsum testimonium,
sed omnes etiam cognatæ species,
quarum genus est mendacium. Ne dicas falsum testimo-
nium de proximo tuo, vel contra proximum tuum. Hoc ne-
gatiuo præcepto comprehenditur affirmatiuum, quod
est, Dicas igitur verum testimonium de vel pro pro-
ximo tuo, id est, sis verax, sis amans discendæ ac cog-
noscendæ veritatis. Veritatis autem nomen accipitur
hic pro veracitate, id est, pro congruentia notitiæ, vel
sermonis cum re de qua est sermo. Verum, est ipse ser-
mo congruens cum re.

l.i: Virtutes huius noni præcepti, additis ea-

main_text.l: Virtus principalis quæ hic præcipitur, est veritas.
1. Veritas, seu potius veracitas, est virtus, qua ve-
ras sententias amamus, inquirimus, amplestimur[?], &
libenter, pro ratione tum officij nostri, tum persona-
rum, locorum, temporum, & aliarum circumstanti-
arum eas profitemur, ac defendimus ad gloriam dei,
& salutem proximi. Facit iste finis ut diabolus non sit
verax, etiam si verum dicat aliquando. Nam verax
est, qui veritatem dicit, & amat, eique studet prop-
ter gloriam Dei, & proximi salutem. Potest & veritas
hoc modo definiri: Veritas est firma electio in volun-
tate, qua constanter amplectimur veras sententias,
dicimus vera, seruamus pacta, & in sermone & gestu
vitamus occultationes insidiosas. Confessio vera præci-
pitur & in hoc, & in tertio præcepto: quomodo sæpe ea-
dem virtus ad obedientiam diuersorum præcepto-
rum rum

page.notes: The woodcut initial N is an ornamental frame with a letter N; the first word is read as "Non". In the italic lines the long s prints like f and is transcribed as plain s (sanctio, conseruatio, testimonium). "amplestimur" is printed in this form; the reading amplestimur is doubtful. Small reference marks appear in the left margin near "Ne dicas" and "tuum" but are not legible enough to transcribe. The final line ends in the catchword "rum", which is repeated as the first word of the next page.
